Definition: properly, a breeze, i.e. (by implication) dusk (when the evening breeze prevails)
BiblicalUsage: Twilight is the hour when the breeze comes up and the light goes, and the Bible sets its most desperate scenes there. David smites the Amalekites from the twilight until the next evening, four lepers rise in the twilight to walk into the Syrian camp, and Job curses the twilight stars of his night.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe twilight is the hour of decision: the lepers walked toward the enemy camp in the half-light, and God had already emptied it. The lepers found an empty camp in the twilight, and David's men found their families still alive to rescue.
